EU-Andean agreement: Applied with Colombia and Peru from 2013 and Ecuador from 2017; routine implementation and evaluation materials.
EU-Mercosur agreement: Trade component concluded in 2019; political agreement on improved Partnership Agreement reached 6 December 2024; interim trade instrument provisionally applied from 1 May 2026.
interpretive relevance: The same broad EU template encounters different political conditions.

EU-Andean agreement: Dedicated Trade and Sustainable Development chapter embedded in implementation committees and evaluation processes.
EU-Mercosur agreement: Dedicated Trade and Sustainable Development chapter with additional 2024 commitments and an expert-panel procedure.
interpretive relevance: Both have sustainability language, but institutional work differs.

EU-Andean agreement: International sustainability commitments are handled through the agreement's TSD and implementation framework.
EU-Mercosur agreement: Paris Agreement is described by the Commission as an essential element of the agreement.
interpretive relevance: The climate commitment is more politically salient in Mercosur.

EU-Andean agreement: Relevant sustainability issues are addressed through implementation dialogue and evaluation; no single land-use controversy dominates the agreement's public trajectory.
EU-Mercosur agreement: Deforestation and land-use change are central to the political economy of the agreement and to the parallel EUDR debate.
interpretive relevance: Sectoral conflict changes the meaning of a common legal template.

EU-Andean agreement: Commission implementation reports and ex post evaluation architecture are visible features of the relationship.
EU-Mercosur agreement: Negotiation texts, explanatory materials, TSD procedures and later implementation are still being assembled; full ex post evidence is not yet available.
interpretive relevance: Evaluation maturity is uneven across the cases.

EU-Andean agreement: Promotional, cooperative and committee-centred governance; enforcement questions remain institutionally mediated.
EU-Mercosur agreement: Formal consultations and an independent panel of experts are available, but ecological transformation still depends on domestic implementation and broader governance.
interpretive relevance: Textual enforceability and transformative capacity are distinct.

EU-Andean agreement: European Commission 2023; Garcia and Gomez Arana 2025; Marín Durán 2020.
EU-Mercosur agreement: European Commission 2020 and 2026; Cesar de Oliveira et al. 2024; Albertoni and Schlegelmilch 2026.
